title: The zero-order Hermite coefficient
statement: Let $n$ be a natural number and let $f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R$ be square-integrable with respect to the $n$-dimensional standard Gaussian measure. The Hermite coefficient of $f$ at the zero multi-index equals the Gaussian integral $\int_{\mathbb R^n} f\,d\gamma^{\otimes n}$.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ is in $L^2$ for the product standard Gaussian measure
